headline.caveat: estimated aggregate: up to ~$14B Texas/Portugal agreement (~104K GB300s at the Ionic Digital site, TX + 12.6K at Start Campus, Portugal) + $6.2B Norway (52K GPUs, Narvik) + UK (Loughton, ~23K GPUs) — ~200K GB300-class GPUs total across four countries

realized_to_date.caveat: deployments over 12–18 months from late 2025; billed amounts not disclosed

nature_md: Cumulative Microsoft–Nscale agreements total roughly $20B+ for approximately 200,000 NVIDIA GB300 GPUs across four countries: (1) the headline up-to-$14B deal for ~104K GB300s at a Texas data center leased from Ionic Digital (240MW scaling toward 1.2GW by 2027) plus ~12.6K GPUs at Start Campus, Sines, Portugal; (2) a $6.2B, 52K-GPU deployment at Narvik, Norway (with Aker); and (3) ~23K GPUs at Loughton, UK under Microsoft's $30B UK pledge. For a company founded in 2024, Microsoft is effectively the entire demand book — the extreme case of neocloud customer concentration, and the anchor for Nscale's mooted 2026 IPO.

accounting.payer_treatment_md: Committed capacity purchases expensed as consumed; lets Microsoft add ~GW-scale GB300 capacity in Europe and Texas without owning the sites.
accounting.payee_treatment_md: Essentially all of Nscale's contracted revenue; underpins its $1.1B Series B, the Mar 2026 raise at $14.6B, and GPU/site financing. Loss or renegotiation of the Microsoft relationship is the single biggest risk to the company.
